label: copy phase: input c, now outputting f (the original bigram c,f)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original tokens or <DEL>. The core case and almost all strong activations: the fed-back input is c and the token being output is f, meaning the original sequence had the bigram c,f. Top examples (about 0.9-1.0 of max) are all c to f, often with f f after it. It is weak or silent when this happens at recall_idx 0-1 (c f at the start of the sequence), and strongest at recall_idx 3-5. The remaining mass, about 25% and mostly low activations, comes from related c/f cases: input f outputting f (bigram ff), input c outputting c (cc), and input c followed by other tokens. It never fires on any input token other than c or f. Precision for c to f with recall_idx >= 2 is about 0.85, and recall is about 0.53 because of these weak c/f neighbours.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=c (+8.18), phase=2 & in_tok=f (+5.30), phase=2 & out_tok=f (+4.87), next_out=f (+4.64), out_tok=f (+4.48), in_tok=c (+4.04). Lower it: recall_idx=1 (-2.65), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.65), orig_idx=-1 (-1.94), next_out=t (-1.85).
